FIVE DATES MUST BE IDENTICAL ACROSS THE FAMILIES THAT SHARE THEIR ARTIFACT, AND ONE RULE DECIDES EACH. Every artifact quoted below I re-read from the bytes this session rather than from a proposal or a synthesis.

(1) THE FLOOR. Law quoted: "Carry the earliest sourced state back to the audit floor. When a phase is primary-sourced at some instant and no primary source names a cutover between the January-2010 floor and that instant, extend it backwards to the floor rather than modelling the interval as sessionless ... Modelling a venue that was demonstrably trading as closed is a worse error than carrying its earliest sourced grid: absence is a claim too." Its precondition is that the MODELLED FAMILY is sourced at some instant, which the knowledge-boundary bullet defines: "A knowledge boundary is the first source that lists the modelled product ... A document only sources a family if that family appears in it." So the floor splits three-two, and it is not a preference: Japan, China and Singapore have members listed WITH A GRID in the oldest artifacts and are carried to the floor as `select_revision` BASELINES asserting no revision row; FTSE Taiwan and the NTR (USD) suite did not exist and stay sessionless below their own launch/first-listing boundaries. The `effective` dates "2010-01-01" printed on the three carried rows are interval labels only — those rows are the baseline argument, carry no date and no citation slot, and govern below the floor too ("Do not add a lower bound to the timelines"). This corrects the Singapore proposal, which printed its floor row as a dated `intersection-start`; the Singapore skeptic quoted the law and is right.

(2) 2013-08-20 — CHINA ONLY, and the reason is the ordering artifact, not a preference. I extracted the wcm/connect fragment (capture 20180711020353) and the portal Trading Hours table (capture 20130820090335) side by side. For Japan every Nikkei row is identical in both (NK/NU 7.45am–2.25pm / 3.15pm–2.00am, NKO 2.30pm, NS 3.25pm/4.15pm, ND 5.55pm/6.45pm); for Singapore MSCI S'pore is identical in both (8.30am–5.10pm / 6.15pm–2.00am, options 5.15pm). Only A50 differs — W "FTSE Xinhua China A50 | 9.00 am - 3.25 pm | 4.10 pm - 2.00 am" against S0 "SGX FTSE China A50 Index Futures | 9.00am to 3.55pm | 4.40pm to 2.00am". So only China's floor interval holds two states and only China splits. W is placed BEFORE S0 on its content, never its capture: its set still names "S&P CNX Nifty", "FTSE Xinhua China A50", "MSCI Asia Apex 50", "MSCI Hong Kong+", no FX and no iron ore. Corroborated: the SAME 2013-08-20 document's seven per-holiday tables print A50 at "9.00am to 3.25pm | 4.10pm to 2.00am" — W's grid — while its normal-week table prints 3.55pm/4.40pm, and every neighbouring contract in those tables matches its own normal-week row (I verified all twelve A50 cells). That is used for ORDER only; per-date data is caller-owned under LAW-HOLIDAY-SCOPE. Its weight is limited and the skeptic is right that the contract set carries the ordering on its own: A50 is the only contract that diverges there and three of the seven dates postdate the capture.

(3) 2017-07-10 — THE STATE-A BOUNDARY, SHARED BY JAPAN, CHINA AND SINGAPORE. The evidence date is the portal capture 20170705000242 (= 2017-07-05 08:02 SGT, twenty-eight minutes before that day's open), whose parsed grid is byte-identical to capture 20170927124017 twelve weeks later; I diffed the eleven equity rows and they match to the character. A CAPTURE TIMESTAMP IS USED HERE AS A KNOWLEDGE BOUNDARY AND NEVER AS A CUTOVER: nothing is claimed to have changed that day, and the real S0→A move is undated. I reject the Japan skeptic's move to 2017-12-26 and I reject both skeptics' framing of the risk as staleness, for three reasons drawn from evidence neither had. First, direction: a served page can be STALE, never EARLY, so a capture is a sound upper bound on a state's onset and can only under-date it — proved twice over in this corpus, by W (a c.2012 state served in 2018) and by SGX's own commodities hours page, which on 2017-09-27 at 13:30 UTC still printed Fuel Oil 380cst and TSI Iron Ore at "2.00 am (following day)" fifty minutes after the derivatives page printed 4.45am for the same contracts (I extracted both; the commodities page contains zero equity-index rows, so it is not a source conflict on any modelled family — it is proof that SGX served stale trees concurrently). Second, the only failure that could make the capture wrong is PREMATURE PUBLICATION, and SGX's own Derivatives Products Description change log now closes it: row 26, issued 2016-04-22, "Equity Index & Dividend Index products T/T+1 gap increased to 15mins" — which describes state A's shape exactly, since A leaves fifteen minutes between the end of each family's closing routine and its T+1 pre-open — and row 27, issued 2016-07-15, "Amendments to NK suite, CH, CHO and CN trading hours". State A most likely began in 2016, so 2017-07-05 already under-reports by a year and cannot be early. Third, the change log's own "Change of Trading Hours" entry is issued 2017-10-05, AFTER both captures, which independently retires the "21 Sep 2017 newsletter" objection. THE KEY MOVES FROM 2017-07-05 (Wed) TO MONDAY 2017-07-10 for boundary hygiene — see (5).

(4) 2020-01-01 — KEPT, ON ALL FIVE KEYS, WITH TWO CONSEQUENTIAL EDITS. The date and the T-session bounds stand on the 2020 edition and the content-api capture 20200109051211. Its citation string "first sourced SGX calendar edition" becomes false once earlier rows exist and must be restated. Its ROUTINES are forced in, on all five keys at once: capture 20200109051211 is identical to the 2019-06-11 payload except that every "Opening: ... - 4.45 am" reads "5.15 am", so it states each family's Pre-Opening/Non-Cancel/Pre-Closing windows INSIDE this row's interval. Adding them to the earlier eras and dropping them here would assert that SGX deleted its own auction routines on New Year's Day 2020, which no source says; adding them to one key and not its siblings would have the crate report an 18:30–18:35 closing auction for NTR that it denies to Japan on the identical payload. All five or none — all five. This retires history.rs's sentence "Routines stay out of the first era deliberately: the calendars state session bounds only, and the circular's 'current' column is the state after the undated Japan move, not before it": the calendars are silent but SGX's content-api is not, and DT/AM 50 now sources the Japan routines on both sides of 2024-11-04. Japan alone splits this era at 2024-11-04; DT/AM 50 enumerates NK, NKO, NR, ND, NU, NS, NC, EJRT, EJP "(collectively, 'Contracts')" and no China, Singapore, Taiwan or NTR contract, so the other four run unbroken to 2025-04-06.

(5) BOUNDARY HYGIENE — WHY TWO ROWS ARE KEYED TO THE FOLLOWING MONDAY. LAW-NO-FABRICATED-DATES: "Day-level revision rows are keyed to the local opening day of the first session they govern, and a day-level revision boundary never splits a running session." `select_revision` picks the profile from the QUERY instant's local date, so a boundary that LENGTHENS or CREATES a wrapping overnight close reports the previous evening's leg running past the close that was in force when it opened. A Wednesday 2017-07-05 key would report Japan/China/Singapore open from 02:00 to 04:45 on that one morning on a leg that opened Tuesday under the 02:00 regime — a false open, which the module's own "DIRECTION OF THE ERROR" note says these rows can no longer produce. Keying to Monday 2017-07-10 removes it exactly, because the rules are Mon-Fri and no leg wraps into a Monday morning (Friday's leg ends Saturday 05:15). Same for the NTR key's sessionless→grid boundary, moved from Wednesday 2018-04-11 to Monday 2018-04-16. Every other boundary here needs no rounding and keeps its artifact's date: 2013-08-20 (Tue) changes only a daytime close, 2019-02-06 (Wed) narrows a T+1 open, 2019-06-11 (Tue) changes only a daytime close, 2020-07-20 is already a Monday. The shipped 2020-01-01 rows have the lengthening shape but are harmless in practice because 1 January is a closed date and "A closed date normally removes its complete trading day, including the prior-evening wrap"; they are left alone.

(6) THE ONE PENDING DECISION THAT WOULD CHANGE THREE OF THESE ROWS, STATED ONCE. Two proposals assert that no SGX-authored channel states a day for the 2019 T+1 extension ("Every SGX-authored channel that could carry a day is closed") and that 2016 is a hole. Both claims are FALSE and must not ship — this is the exact "'Unsourced' means 'not worked up', never 'no source exists'" failure the law was written about. SGX's Derivatives Products Description change log, downloaded live from api2.sgx.com and held at raw/catalogue/v17.6/, states day-level effective dates in the same form as the two circulars this crate already trusts. I re-parsed the OOXML independently (zipfile + ElementTree, sheet1.xml, mergeCells = 0) and confirm verbatim: r76, issued 2019-05-21, v6.1, single cell — "Amended trading hours for SGP, SGPO and ST eff 10 Jun"; r87–r89 inside one border-partitioned entry whose dated row r90 is 2019-10-07 v6.9 — "Effective 11 Nov:" / "Editorial change Contracts_mainmenu:" / "(T+1) session Closing hours to 5:15am all T+1 traded contracts"; and the calibrators r163, issued 2024-11-04, "Amend trading hours of SGX Nikkei Derivatives and SGX FTSE Blossom Japan Index Futures (eff 4 Nov)" = DT/AM 50, and r170, issued 2025-03-19, "(eff 7 Apr)" = DT/AM 15. Admitting this channel is recorded in the store as DECISION PENDING with the maintainer (2026-09-06-catalogue-changelog-REVERSAL.md, issue #45), and the brief I was given states the 04:45→05:15 move has no day, so I build the conservative table — but the refinement is mechanical, not a re-derivation: accepting the channel replaces Singapore's two rows 2019-02-06 and 2019-06-11 with ONE dated cutover at Monday 2019-06-10 (r76 needs no scoping inference at all and is the strongest of the three), and moves the 05:15 T+1 close on ALL FIVE keys from 2020-01-01 back to Monday 2019-11-11 (r89, which needs the one interpretive step of scoping a header row to the items below it inside a single file-encoded entry). Rows 26 and 27 state no effective day and therefore date nothing either way; they only prove the 2016 negative false.

per_family.floor_decision: (i) CARRIED, and for this family the two candidate constructions coincide exactly, so no choice has to be defended. LAW quoted in full: "Carry the earliest sourced state back to the audit floor. When a phase is primary-sourced at some instant and no primary source names a cutover between the January-2010 floor and that instant, extend it backwards to the floor rather than modelling the interval as sessionless. This asserts *no* revision row, so it does not fabricate a date - it declines to invent one, exactly as ICE Sugar's August-2011 baseline is carried back. Modelling a venue that was demonstrably trading as closed is a worse error than carrying its earliest sourced grid: absence is a claim too." And: "Prefer the sourced intersection to omission ... serve the window that holds under *every* sourced state and withhold only the disputed remainder." INTERSECTION COMPUTED BOUND BY BOUND, S0 ∩ A: T open max(07:45,07:30)=07:45 to min(14:25,14:25)=14:25; T+1 open max(15:15,14:55)=15:15 to min(02:00,04:45)=02:00. That is S0 exactly, because A strictly contains S0 in both phases. So carry-back of the earliest sourced state and the sourced intersection with the next state produce the same table; nothing is withheld and nothing extra is asserted. WHY NOT SESSIONLESS: the existing note's stated reason — "no edition of the calendar survives before it" — is now known false. The 2018 (Apr) and 2019 editions are still served live from api2.sgx.com and SGX's own hours page sits in the archive from 2013. Under "'Unsourced' means 'not worked up', never 'no source exists' ... A sessionless era is a safe answer either way, but the stated reason has to be true", the blackout must go. W TREATED BY ITS CONTENT DATE, AND WHAT THAT IMPLIES: its contract set places it around 2012, and its five Nikkei rows are identical to S0's, so placing it at its content date merely pushes the attestation of the S0 grid back a further year and STRENGTHENS the carry-back; placing it at its 2018 capture date would manufacture a mid-2018 reversion to 02:00 that the 2018 (Apr) calendar, the 2019 calendar and the 2019 content-api all contradict. The 02:00-versus-04:45 ordering problem is therefore inert for Japan. RESIDUAL RISK EITHER WAY: carrying over-reports the T+1 close by up to one hour for most of 2010 on third-party press attestation (mondovisione 2010-01-08, close 01:00 effective 2010-01-11; thetradenews 2010-08-17, 01:00→02:00 on 2010-08-30), and may over-report the whole T+1 leg before 2010-01-11 — the law anticipates exactly this and says carry anyway and state it. Not carrying would report a demonstrably trading market closed for sixteen years, including the two intervals where SGX's own pages state the grid. The first error is bounded at one hour a night in one year; the second is total.

AGENTS.md: "'Unsourced' means 'not worked up', never 'no source exists'. Say a row is unmodelled before an era and say what would close it; do not write that nothing survives unless the predecessor channels have actually been searched." The proposal wrote "no artifact states the family's HOURS before the 2021 edition" and "The captures in hand stop at 2020-01-09". The store's own `raw/intermediate-2019-state/cdx_contentapi.txt` enumerates `derivatives_products_list` captures at 20200715061901, 20201104145146 and 20201206215049 — I confirmed those three rows in the index and then decoded all three payloads: every one lists TWN with the full grid AND the full routine set, and two of the three post-date the launch. The channel was enumerated and never opened; only the older `limit:10000` queryId variant had been fetched, and Wayback answers that URL at a 2020-11 timestamp with a 302 to the June capture, which is how a searched channel can read as exhausted while it is not. WHY THIS IS STILL A KNOWLEDGE BOUNDARY AND NOT A CUTOVER: the family did not exist before it, exactly as a launch day separates a venue from its pre-launch closure. THE GRID AND ROUTINES ARE THE SOURCED INTERSECTION OVER THE WHOLE INTERVAL, and it is degenerate: T 08:45–13:45 and T+1 14:15–05:15 are identical in the three 2020 payloads and in the 2020-... editions history.rs already tabulates (2021-01, 2021-07, 2022-06, 2024, 2025-01), and DT/AM 15 of 2025 restates the same T routine 08:30/08:43/08:45, the same closing routine 13:45/13:49/13:50 as unchanged, and 14:05/14:13/14:15 as the pre-2025 current T+1 routine. per_family.floor_decision: (ii) SESSIONLESS from the January-2010 floor to 2020-07-19, and for a reason stronger than "not worked up": the modelled contracts did not exist. It reads "Modelling a venue that was demonstrably trading as closed is a worse error than carrying its earliest sourced grid" — the premise is DEMONSTRABLY TRADING, and SGX FTSE Taiwan Index Futures demonstrably was not: SGX's release of 1 July 2020 is future-tense ("SGX is launching SGX FTSE Taiwan Index futures"), SGX's own product catalogue archived 2 June 2020 lists 251 contract codes and none of them is this family, and ten hours-bearing SGX artifacts spanning 2013-08-20 to 2020-01-09 list only the MSCI predecessors and the NTR sibling. rows.why: KNOWLEDGE BOUNDARY, not a claimed change: no source says anything happened that day. LAW quoted: "A knowledge boundary is the first source that lists the modelled product, not merely the earliest source that survives. A document only sources a family if that family appears in it." The first source that both lists this family and states a grid is the 2018 (Apr) calendar, which puts fourteen rows including NSG on 7.25am–6.30pm / 7.00pm–4.45am. WHY 2018-04-16 AND NOT 2018-01-01: I reject the proposal's date. It is derived from the edition's filename year, which the brief forbids ("Do NOT infer a day from a month, a filename, a directory, or a capture"), it reaches 101 days behind the document's own date, and the proposal justified it with the edition's "accurate as of 26 December 2017" line while its own open question disowned that line as unreconciled boilerplate against an April creation date. The artifact's own day-level date is 2018-04-11. AND A REASON NEITHER SKEPTIC HAD DECIDES BETWEEN THE CANDIDATES: SGX's own Derivatives Products Description change log, row 51, issued 2017-12-29, v3.6, reads "Change of Trading Hours for EM and NTR suite" — an undated NTR hours change at the turn of 2017/2018. Keying at 2018-01-01 or 2017-12-26 would carry the 2018 grid back across that sourced change with no second state to intersect; keying at the document's own date sits safely after it. The row is then rounded forward to Monday 2018-04-16 because it CREATES a wrapping overnight close where the profile was previously sessionless: a Wednesday key would report the family open from 00:00 to 04:45 on that morning on a leg that never opened. LAW-NO-FABRICATED-DATES: "a day-level revision boundary never splits a running session." T+1 CLOSE 04:45 IS THE SOURCED INTERSECTION over the tail of this era: state B is last witnessed at 04:45 by content-api revisit 20190621080419 and state C at 05:15 by the 2020 edition, and the changeover is undated in the channels this row cites, so bound by bound the T+1 open is 19:00 under both and the close is min(04:45, 05:15) = 04:45; the disputed half-hour waits on the next row, exactly as CME's Sunday Pre-Open withholds 16:00–16:15. ROUTINES ARE NEW relative to the shipped empty sets and come from content-api 20190204200905, carried back inside an era in which no sourced bound moves; the 2018 edition does not contradict them, it excludes them by footnote ("Timings exclude pre-opening and pre-closing routines, the respective non-cancel periods as well as the respective order-cancellation session states where applicable"). SGX's own Titan DTDC Factsheet Dec 2019 corroborates the 07:10 queue onset market-wide ("commencing at the start of the Asian trading contract pre-opening at 7.10am") — a market-wide claim, not a statement about this family, and cited as such.

law_amendment_needed:
TWO BULLETS IN AGENTS.md's "Modeling conventions" MUST CHANGE BEFORE THESE ROWS ARE LEGAL. Both are one-paragraph edits; neither touches a named LAW.

(1) THE KNOWLEDGE-BOUNDARY BULLET'S WORKED EXAMPLE IS NOW STALE AND CONTRADICTS THE DATA. Moving the FTSE Taiwan row from 2021-01-01 to 2020-07-20 falsifies the illustration the bullet uses, while leaving the principle it teaches untouched — indeed the principle is what forces the move. Leaving the text as it stands would have the repository's stated law contradict its own schedule table. Replace the bullet in full with:

"- **A knowledge boundary is the first source that lists the modelled product,** not merely the earliest source that survives. A document only sources a family if that family appears in it. SGX's FTSE Taiwan suite is the worked example, and it is also the worked example of getting this half-right: the 2020 calendar edition is the earliest calendar that survives, but it lists only the MSCI Taiwan predecessors, so the row cannot start there — and the row does not start at the 2021 edition either, because SGX's own product catalogue lists the FTSE suite with a full grid from July 2020, five months before that edition. The predecessor's hours were identical, which is exactly why the first half is easy to miss; and one channel's earliest surviving document is not the family's earliest source, which is exactly why the second half is easy to miss. Check the contract set, not just the grid, before keying a row to an edition — and check the other channels before concluding an edition is the earliest source at all."

(2) A KNOWLEDGE BOUNDARY MAY WIDEN WHAT IS SERVED AND MAY NEVER NARROW IT. The China floor row deliberately withholds twenty minutes of T+1 that both states sourced in its interval hold open, which a naive reading of "Prefer the sourced intersection to omission" forbids; the reason it is right is not stated anywhere in AGENTS.md today, and the next reader will re-derive the proposal's version and encode an unsourced closure at a Wayback timestamp. Add, immediately after the "Prefer the sourced intersection to omission" bullet:

"- **A knowledge boundary may only widen.** Intersecting per interval can make a bound move *inward* at a boundary that asserts no change — three sourced states in sequence, with the middle one directly witnessed on a date, will do it. Do not encode that. Knowledge does not shrink: a boundary that widens says 'from here we have sourced this much', and one that narrows says a window that was open became closed, which is a claim about the market that LAW-NO-FABRICATED-DATES requires a stated day for and which would enter `HISTORICAL_CUTOVERS` reading as sourced. Where the per-interval intersections would narrow a bound, hold that bound at its narrowest value across the whole undated span and withhold the disputed remainder from the earlier interval, exactly as CME's Sunday Pre-Open withholds 16:00-16:15 rather than granting it early and withdrawing it at the capture that first shows the later state. SGX's FTSE China A50 is the worked example: its T+1 open is sourced at 16:10, 16:40 and 17:00 in three undated states, so 17:00 is served from the floor and only the T close, which widens, is keyed at the boundaries.
  The same asymmetry decides the day. A day-level row that lengthens or creates a wrapping overnight close is keyed to the following Monday, because `select_revision` reads the query instant's local date and a mid-week key would report the previous evening's leg running past the close that was in force when it opened — which is the running session LAW-NO-FABRICATED-DATES says a boundary must not split. A row that changes only daytime bounds, or that narrows an overnight open, keeps its artifact's own date."

NOTHING ELSE NEEDS AMENDING. The carry-back bullet, the sourced-intersection bullet, the "'Unsourced' means 'not worked up'" bullet, "Executable windows are the priority", "Product-neutral family selection", LAW-NO-FABRICATED-DATES, LAW-PRIMARY-SOURCES, LAW-PUBLIC-SOURCES, LAW-HOLIDAY-SCOPE and the floor convention all cover these rows as written, and several of them are quoted in the tables above doing exactly the work they were written for.
